newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Centromin says still committed to silver.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Centromin says still committed to silver.

text.p: Peru's leading silver producer, state-run Centromin, said the metal's price falls would not affect its output.
"We are continuing production at the same level as before. There is no move to scale down output," Centromin spokesman Enrique Olivares said.
According to latest figures, Centromin produced 188.3 tonnes of silver in the first five months, 1.29 percent lower than its production over the same period last year.
The slight fall was due to "normal variations" rather than any changes in strategy, Olivares said.
Centromin's five-month silver production represented 22 percent of total national output of 850.7 tonnes.
Olivares added, however, that Centromin, which operates polymetallic mines, had made zinc its priority for this year due to its rosy price prospects.
"We are concentrating efforts on zinc, but this has not impacted silver production," he said.
Centromin is also Peru's leading zinc producer, with five- month output of 131,348 tonnes, up 9.12 percent from 120,366 tonnes in the same period last year.
